notes: Focused regression prompts for correctness fixes in v1.5.1. These are versioned prompts and grading assertions, not claims of a completed comparative benchmark.

evals.name: bubble-tea-cleanup-review
evals.prompt: Review this Bubble Tea shutdown pattern before I ship it: `p := tea.NewProgram(model); defer p.RestoreTerminal(); _, err := p.Run(); return err`. I added the defer to make sure a panic cannot leave the terminal broken. Is this correct, and what should I use instead?
assertions: Says the defer is incorrect and should be removed
Explains that RestoreTerminal resumes Bubble Tea terminal mode after ReleaseTerminal rather than performing final shell cleanup
Explains that Bubble Tea's normal Run lifecycle and default panic handling clean up the terminal
Only recommends a custom outer cleanup boundary when bypassing or disabling the framework-managed path

evals.name: ratatui-color-eyre-hook-order
evals.prompt: In a current Ratatui app using color-eyre, should I install a terminal-restoring panic hook before color_eyre::install(), after it, or rely on ratatui::run/init? Show the correct ordering and explain when a custom hook is actually needed.
assertions: Prefers Ratatui's managed run/init/try_init restoration behavior
Installs color_eyre before Ratatui initialization so Ratatui wraps the reporting hook and restores first
Limits a custom restoration hook to manual terminal construction/setup
Does not stack a redundant custom restoration wrapper on top of ratatui::run or ratatui::init

evals.name: responsive-minimum-contract
evals.prompt: My TUI supports a useful single-pane mode at 60 columns, but our docs say every terminal below 80 columns should show `Terminal too small — need 80x24`. Should I keep that as the standard minimum?
assertions: Treats 80x24 as a compatibility test baseline rather than a universal hard minimum
Recommends an application-specific minimum derived from the smallest usable layout
Requires the too-small message to name the actual tested minimum
Describes a concrete degradation path from multi-pane to single-pane before refusing to render

evals.name: fzf-inline-default-correction
evals.prompt: I'm citing fzf as proof that fuzzy pickers render inline by default. Is that accurate? I want a bounded picker that preserves the invoking command and prints the chosen item for command substitution.
assertions: Corrects the claim: fzf defaults to full-screen rendering
Names fzf --height as the explicit bounded inline pattern
Recommends inline rendering for this requested receipt/scrollback contract without making it universal
Separates UI output from the selected value so command substitution remains scriptable

evals.name: owo-colors-no-color-policy
evals.prompt: I'm using owo-colors directly in a Rust CLI. Can I state that it automatically honors NO_COLOR, or do I need to do something?
assertions: Does not claim direct owo-colors styling automatically suppresses color
Names the supports-colors feature and if_supports_color path or recommends an explicit equivalent policy
Accounts for NO_COLOR and non-TTY output
Keeps an explicit force-color override as an application-level policy decision and defines precedence when force and disable signals conflict
